34.0.0.en: 1- I will bless the LORD at all times: his praise shall continually be in my mouth.

34.0.1.en: 1- David felt the hand of God that had rescued him from death, so he lifted up his heart in thanksgiving and praise, and felt that God's work with him called him to praise Him throughout his life, indeed at all times, perhaps to repay God something of what He deserves; it is gratitude, and a sense and appreciation of God's grace.

34.0.2.en: 2- The constant praise results from David's sense of God's continual care for him; indeed it is a feeling of God's being with him, and a desire on David's part to enjoy His presence always. Therefore he praises Him at all times, in the time of affliction or in the time of ease, declaring that God is the secret of his happiness and joy.

34.0.3.en: 3- Perhaps David realized that the work of the heavenly ones is praise, so he wanted to share with them in praising God, out of longing for eternity and in preparation for it, and enjoying it as a pledge while still on earth.

34.0.4.en: 4- Pleasing God in every work that man does, and not only in the words of praise, is obedience to God and occupation with Him, and this is counted as continual praise throughout the day.

34.1.0.en: 2- My soul shall make her boast in the LORD: the humble shall hear thereof, and be glad.

34.1.1.en: 1- Every person needs to boast in something. The children of God boast in God, but the children of the world boast in themselves, and this leads to pride, or they boast in evil, and so go on further in their sins.

34.1.2.en: 2- Boasting in the Lord gives man confidence in himself, because God is with him, fills his heart with peace, and moves him to bear all responsibilities and to succeed in them.

34.1.3.en: 3- It is easy for the humble man to boast in God and glorify Him at all times, and he feels God's gifts, so he thanks Him and praises Him continually; but God has no need of people's boasting in Him, because He is perfect in Himself.

34.1.4.en: 4- When the humble, who are the gentle and full of peace, hear of the humble David's boasting in God his Savior, they rejoice; for the humble boast in God, and they rejoice when they hear of any person who boasts in God, and they are even stirred and increase in boasting in God and praising Him.

34.1.5.en: 5- Boasting in God and glorifying Him fills the heart with joy, for it feels God's love, and even His being with it, so it holds fast to Him and increases its enjoyment of fellowship with Him.

34.1.6.en: 6- Man boasts in God, but as for himself he boasts in his weaknesses, which lead to the intervention of God, who completes his lack and is glorified in him, as happened with the Apostle Paul (2 Cor 11:30).

34.2.0.en: 3- O magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt his name together.

34.2.1.en: 1- When David's heart was occupied with praising God, he felt responsible for others, so he called them to magnify the Lord and praise Him with him, that they might enjoy with him being in His presence.

34.2.2.en: 2- David's call to the children of God to glorify and praise Him shows David's faith in communal worship in the tabernacle of meeting, which signifies the Church of the New Testament.

34.2.3.en: 3- Exalting the name of God is not an addition to His holy name, because He is perfect, but it is a showing forth of His glory and thanksgiving for His kindnesses, so that man enjoys the knowledge of God and delights in fellowship with Him.

34.2.4.en: 4- Magnifying God is accomplished in five stages, which are:

34.2.5.en: A - In the mind and thought, that is, thinking of God's greatness and His works.

34.2.6.en: B - In the heart, when man's feelings are moved with love toward God.

34.2.7.en: C - In speech, with words of praise and thanksgiving.

34.2.8.en: D - In works, by obeying His commandments, especially in affliction.

34.2.9.en: E - In calling others to share in glorifying Him.

34.2.10.en: How beautiful is the praise of God! For when you join with those who praise, you are lifted up to heaven and are with the angels and the saints. So do not deprive yourself of praise every day, even with a small part of the Midnight Praise.

34.3.s.en: (2) Blessings for those who seek Him

34.3.0.en: 4- I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.

34.3.1.en: 1- David's faith appears when he recalls what confirms his faith, namely the situations in which he sought God and He answered him. Whenever man's faith is confirmed he is encouraged, so he asks of God with confidence at every time, and trusts that God hears him and answers him.

34.3.2.en: 2- God does not answer because people do not ask, or ask with doubt, or ask for bad things, or in their ignorance do not know what is to their advantage, or their good. Indeed the good may be the opposite of what they asked.

34.3.3.en: 3- In affliction Satan fights with doubts and fears within man. So when God answers and rescues man from his enemies, Satan can continue in his casting of doubts, but God's power appeared in driving all these fears out of David's heart.

34.4.0.en: 5- They looked unto him, and were lightened: and their faces were not ashamed.

34.4.1.en: 1- David turns here from speaking about himself to speaking about the children of God, who seek Him and take refuge in Him in their afflictions, to affirm that he is not the only one who lives with God, but many enjoy fellowship with God.

34.4.2.en: 2- When the children of God ask of Him in affliction, they receive a great blessing, which is their being with God, so their hearts and minds are enlightened, they know God and are filled with peace, and they receive the ability to discern the truth in order to walk in it. This is greater than the removal of the affliction. The affliction may remain for a time, but they will have received spiritual enlightenment.

34.4.3.en: 3- The spiritual enlightenment that those who seek the Lord receive gives them boldness and peace, so they approach with confidence in prayer, and ask and press upon God, and their relationship with Him increases, and God also gives them favor in the eyes of those around them. And in the end He makes them succeed and grow spiritually, so they are not put to shame.

34.5.0.en: 6- This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.

34.5.1.en: 1- By the poor man David means himself, that is, the humble one who cried to God, and He heard him and answered him, because God loves the humble, and listens to them attentively and answers them quickly.

34.5.2.en: 2- The poor man suffers many afflictions and hardships, but God loves him and hastens to him, and He is able to deliver him from all his hardships, so God is glorified in him, and he thanks God and glorifies Him.

34.5.3.en: 3- Perhaps David, in the spirit of prophecy, speaks of King Hezekiah, the poor man who implored God in humility to rescue him from the hands of Sennacherib, and God heard him and answered him, and sent His angel, who destroyed the army of Sennacherib and rescued his people from his hands.

34.5.4.en: 4- The angels hear David's words and rejoice and support them, because heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents more than over ninety and nine just persons who need no repentance. The angels rejoice over the humble who cry to God, so He hastens to them and rescues them from their enemies. Perhaps David felt that the angels repeat this verse in heaven in joy at the salvation of sinners.

34.6.0.en: 7- The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.

34.6.1.en: 1- God cares for those who fear Him, and by this David declared his faith and reliance on God: God cannot leave him, but delivers him from all his afflictions.

34.6.2.en: 2- The demons help the wicked and stir them up against the righteous who fear God; therefore God must support His holy children, so He sends them angels to protect them, and these are stronger than the demons, because they have the power of God with them.

34.6.3.en: 3- God has assigned an angel to everyone who fears Him, and he never leaves him; for he encamps round about those who fear Him, that is, he remains steadfast in guarding the one whom God has charged him to look after, and he alerts him and encourages him in the spiritual life.

34.7.0.en: 8- O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.

34.7.1.en: 1- Hearing reports about God is not enough; therefore the prophet David calls all who love God to come forward, to gain practical experience in knowing God by tasting His sweetness. Just as talking about honey is not enough to know its sweetness, but it must be tasted, so too God's sweetness is known only by tasting it through prayer and reading.

34.7.2.en: 2- If man tastes God's sweetness he will need to see Him, that is, to contemplate Him, and God reveals to him something new of Himself, and he enjoys new depths in fellowship with Him.

34.7.3.en: 3- Whoever tastes God's sweetness knows the extent of His fatherhood and His power, so he relies on Him and is at rest in His embrace, and enjoys an inexpressible inward peace that encourages him to continue tasting God's sweetness and contemplating Him.

34.7.4.en: 4- This tasting and contemplation continue and grow throughout life, then deepen further upon entering eternity, and there man continues to enjoy tasting God in a new way whose beauty cannot be expressed, so that whoever has experienced it cannot express the extent of its sweetness, like the Apostle Paul, who could only say of God's sweetness in eternity that it is what "eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man" (1 Cor 2:9).

34.8.0.en: 9- O fear the LORD, ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.

34.8.1.en: 10- The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger: but they that seek the LORD shall not want any good thing.

34.8.3.en: 1- Why does David ask the saints to fear God and revere Him? Because the saints care about the worship of God, so they know Him and fear Him. This is a call to go deeper in the fear of God as their knowledge of God and their attachment to Him increase, for God reveals to them His greatness and how hard it is to be far from Him, as St. Pachomius, the father of koinonia, desired to see hell, and he saw it, and his hatred of sin increased, and the fear of God also increased in his heart.

34.8.4.en: 2- The saints always look to God, and consequently His fear is established in them, and this moves them to grow in the life of godliness.

34.8.5.en: 3- Whoever looks to God and suffers much in God is satisfied by Him, so he is not exposed to hunger and need. The meaning is not material need, though God provides that for His children, but rather spiritual need; they do not suffer spiritual want, that is, they are constantly satisfied by God.

34.8.6.en: 4- A thirst for righteousness is generated within the children of God who fear Him, for the fear of God purifies them from sin, so their longing for God increases; but this hunger is not accompanied by a sense of deprivation, but on the contrary by a spiritual satisfaction that works in them with constant longings for more and more satisfaction.

34.8.7.en: 5- All creatures are exposed to want and need, even the young lions; for the lion is the king of the forest, yet his young can be in need of food. But whoever seeks God cannot be in need, since God Himself cares for him and provides for his needs.

34.8.8.en: In summary, God's blessings to those who seek Him are:

34.8.12.en: 4- He surrounds us with His angels (v. 7).

34.8.14.en: 6- He supplies our needs (vv. 9, 10). And in order to receive these blessings we must turn to God with the following:

34.8.21.en: God is very rich, and He is ready to satisfy you from His riches as much as you ask, so do not be distracted from Him by the passing things of this world, or let your requests be only material requests; but seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, that is, let God reign over your heart and satisfy you, that you may enjoy His inexpressible fellowship.

34.9.0.en: 11- Come, ye children, hearken unto me: I will teach you the fear of the LORD.

34.9.1.en: 12- What man is he that desireth life, and loveth many days, that he may see good?

34.9.2.en: 1- These two verses show David's concern for the fear of God, which is the entrance to the spiritual life and to all blessings on earth and in heaven.

34.9.3.en: 2- The fear of God is a very important matter and needs to be learned, and we see here David's concern to teach his people this fear, which needs definite exercises in order to acquire it.

34.9.4.en: 3- No one cares to learn the fear of God except His sons and those who love Him, since they are bound to Him and want to feel His awe in order to go deeper in knowing Him; as for those far from God, the matter does not concern them.

34.9.5.en: 4- David calls those who want to learn "children" for the following reasons:

34.9.6.en: A - It is a word full of love, for the father loves his children and wants them to be in the best condition.

34.9.7.en: B - The son feels that he is smaller than his father and needs to learn, so he comes to hear and obey what he learns from him.

34.9.8.en: 5- The blessings of acquiring the fear of God are:

34.9.10.en: B - The days of his enjoyment of fellowship with God increase.

34.9.11.en: C - He receives many good things, beginning on earth and extending into eternity in an inexpressible way.

34.9.12.en: 6- The life that man desires is not meant to be life on earth and many days in one's lifetime, because animals, trees and inanimate creatures such as the stars enjoy these. But man is distinguished from all of them in that he receives eternal life, whose days are without number, so the many days are meant to be eternity, and there he enjoys inexpressible good things.

34.10.0.en: 13- Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile.

34.10.1.en: 14- Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.

34.10.2.en: 1- To acquire the fear of God one must keep away from evil, whether in speech or in deed: "Keep thy tongue" - "depart" (that is, keep away). For evil blinds man's insight so that he does not see God and does not hear His voice, and the fear of God grows weak in the heart. This calls for keeping away from association with the wicked who cause stumbling.

34.10.3.en: 2- It is also necessary, on the negative side, to keep away from guile, because in it is the twisting of the heart, which appears in deceitful words or works. God does not accept guile and lying, so guile must be rejected in order to acquire the fear of God.

34.10.4.en: 3- On the positive side, doing good establishes the fear of God; for how can I find someone in need and not help him? And what shall I say to God who sees me? One who fears God seeks all works of goodness, as Christ went about everywhere doing good (Acts 10:38).

34.10.5.en: 4- Whoever fears God seeks peace, to be a son of the God of peace, who is Christ our God, who made peace between heaven and earth, and also between the Jews and the Gentiles, and likewise between the spirit and the body.

34.10.6.en: If only you would seek peace, for it is the most precious gift that you receive from God and offer to those around you, whatever concessions you make, for nothing equals peace. Your right to peace is more precious than all material and moral rights. And in the end the fear of God and His love are established in your heart.

34.11.0.en: 15- The eyes of the LORD are upon the righteous, and his ears are open unto their cry.

34.11.1.en: 1- The eyes of the Lord mean His watching, His care and His concern. And because God is the searcher of hearts and reins, His eyes see the inside of His children, and not only the outside. All this is to supply their spiritual, psychological and bodily needs.

34.11.2.en: 2- God is concerned for and cares for the righteous, because they are His children who obey His commandments, and their good works confirm their sonship to Him. So God gives them special care, more than the rest of mankind.

34.11.3.en: 3- The cry of the righteous quickly reaches the ears of God, that is, God is deeply moved by the needs of His children and their suffering, so He hastens to their aid. And if He is sometimes long-suffering and delays the answer, it is so that their repentance may be completed, and His blessings that He pours out on them may increase, because of their endurance and their love for Him.

34.11.4.en: 4- God leaves man freedom of movement and choice of what suits him, but He watches over him with His eye and listens to his words and his cry, as a mother cares for her child. This shows God's concern for man's freedom, and also His concern for his care, which gives man security.

34.12.0.en: 16- The face of the LORD is against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

34.12.1.en: 1- The face of the Lord here means His anger at the wicked and His judgment of their deeds. He is against them and not with them, just as His eyes looked from afar with tenderness, love and care upon the righteous.

34.12.2.en: 2- The wicked's continuing in their evils means that they are walking toward their certain destruction as a result of God's anger against them, for the wages of sin is death.

34.13.0.en: 17- The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.

34.13.1.en: 1- Those are the righteous of whom he spoke in v. 15. When afflictions met them, they cried to God, because they believe that He is their God and their Father, who provides for all their needs and solves all their problems. Crying means severe need, for their only refuge is God.

34.13.2.en: 2- God's hearing the cry of His children means not mere ordinary listening, but concern for their requests and full readiness to rescue them from their troubles and supply all their needs. But it is at the proper time which He sees to be for their good, for He is able to do everything at any time, but He chooses what is most suitable for their spiritual salvation.

34.13.3.en: 3- God rescued His children from all their hardships, because He is able to do everything; but if He postpones rescuing them materially for their benefit, He must rescue them spiritually and psychologically, for He gives them patience, and even comfort and spiritual delight during the affliction, so that His children hardly feel the weariness of the affliction because of the abundance of consolations, in proportion to how much they cry to God and continue to hold fast to Him.

34.14.0.en: 18- The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

34.14.1.en: 1- He tells us in this verse about God's feelings toward His children who cry to Him, and declares His special concern for the humble, and that He is near to them, that is, He feels their troubles and is ready to support them in all that they suffer.

34.14.2.en: 2- The broken-hearted is the one who accepts the afflictions that God allows, and even feels that they are because of his many sins, so he does not murmur or blame God. But he humbles himself before Him, seeking His help, and so receives the overflow of God's mercies.

34.14.3.en: 3- The broken-hearted also accepts God's chastenings, which lead him to repentance and the reform of his life. And by his humility and obedience he fulfills God's plan for his salvation, so God supports him and rejoices in him.

34.14.4.en: 4- The broken-hearted is the servant, the father and the shepherd who is moved by the fall of his beloved ones into sin, so he prays for them and strives that God may remove from them the circumstances that help toward sin. When God sees his prayers, fasts and prostrations (metanoias) for them, He declares that He is very near to him, appreciates his labors, and rewards him for them with countless blessings.

34.14.5.en: 5- God is exceedingly high above all people, so if man exalts himself in his thinking, searching for God and relying on his mind, he feels that God becomes more and more exalted the nearer he approaches Him, until in the end he feels his inability to know God. But if he is crushed in great humility and his heart is broken before God, then God has compassion on him, draws near to him and reveals Himself to him. He is near to the humble who seek Him, and He reveals His secrets to them.

34.14.6.en: 6- The contrite in spirit is the one who gives his life for God. Contrition means that nothing is left to him in himself, for he has been crushed and ground and become dust, and then he receives blessings and a salvation that surpasses the mind. For when he becomes nothing, everything is in God, who fills him and satisfies him and gives him complete salvation. This is the truly humble.

34.15.0.en: 19- Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all.

34.15.1.en: 20- He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.

34.15.2.en: 1- Afflictions pass over all people, the righteous and the wicked, but they are more upon the righteous, because they are different from the people of the world, so Satan opposes them; but in the end complete happiness awaits the righteous in the Kingdom, while eternal torment awaits the wicked. In addition, there are God's consolations to the righteous during all their afflictions, and His support of them, so they do not grow weary of the afflictions.

34.15.3.en: 2- God delivers the righteous from all afflictions: He removes them from him, ends them, and compensates him with many blessings. In addition, He delivers him during the affliction through his sense that God is with him, so his heart rejoices, as it was with the three youths in the midst of the furnace.

34.15.4.en: 3- The bones are the strongest thing in man, around which the flesh, muscles and skin gather, so they signify the spirit within the body, which believes in God and all His commandments and spiritual principles. Afflictions cannot change or break the faith of the children of God, even if the body is exposed to torments or afflictions.

34.15.5.en: 4- God allows afflictions for His children, and despite their many number He delivers them from them all, and does not allow one of their bones to be broken, so He keeps them in faith in Him, however great their bodily and psychological suffering.

34.15.6.en: 5- This verse was fulfilled in Christ on the Cross, when not a bone of Him was broken, to signify the firmness of His mind, and the salvation that He offers us by His death and resurrection.

34.15.7.en: 6- If Christ is the Head and the Church is His body, then the bones are the believers in Him. God keeps all of these so that they are not broken, but establishes His children in His Church and gives them eternal salvation. This psalm is prayed at the Third Hour, in which the Holy Spirit descended upon the Church, and in this hour it was founded.

34.16.0.en: 21- Evil shall slay the wicked: and they that hate the righteous shall be punished.

34.16.1.en: 1- The sins that man commits harm him first before they harm others, for they tense his nerves and fill his heart with spite, so his blood changes and is filled with poisons that harm his body. And as these sins continue, man is affected and dies because of his evils.

34.16.2.en: 2- If sins affect man in his life on earth, they affect him even more in the other life, for eternal torment awaits him, which is hard to grasp.

34.16.3.en: 3- Also the wicked man, because of his evils, sometimes dies in a hideous way, like the death of Herod and also of King Antiochus, whom worms ate (Acts 12:23; 2 Macc 9:8, 9) while they were alive, and likewise the death of Arius, when his bowels came out of him as he entered the latrine.

34.16.4.en: 4- Although the righteous endures the one who hates him, and God is long-suffering toward these wicked, in the end those who hate the righteous must be punished, because they rejected righteousness, their hearts were filled with hatred, and they were proud, relying on their strength. In the end nothing awaits them but divine punishment in eternal torment, in addition to various earthly punishments, such as the punishment of the Jews who crucified Christ by the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70, and the killing of huge numbers of them.

34.17.0.en: 22- The LORD redeemeth the soul of his servants: and none of them that trust in him shall be punished.

34.17.1.en: 1- God redeemed His servants who believe in Him by His Incarnation in the fullness of time and His death on the Cross for them.

34.17.2.en: 2- Although the children of God sin and deserve punishment, and the penalty of sin is death, God redeems them by giving them life, while others die because of their persistence in evil, as the children of Israel sinned in Egypt and worshiped idols, so He allowed them to be humiliated in forced labor, but He struck the Egyptians with the ten plagues, and then Pharaoh and all his army were drowned in the Red Sea, while the children of Israel crossed in safety to the wilderness of Sinai. Likewise God redeemed Isaac with a ram because of Abraham's faith and his love for God.

34.17.3.en: 3- Every person who has trusted in God, despite his many sins, God accepts his repentance for the sake of his faith and his reliance on Him, so he is not punished in the other life, but enters the Kingdom of Heaven.

34.17.4.en: God cares for you throughout your life, so do not be alarmed by afflictions, because they are temporary, and God keeps you during them, supports you and comforts your heart.

34.17.5.en: God is my Savior from my enemies. By David. "Plead my cause, O LORD, with them that strive with me" ... (v. 1) Introduction:

34.17.6.en: 1- Its author is David the prophet.

34.17.7.en: 2- When he wrote it: when he was suffering from Saul's pursuit of him.

34.17.8.en: 3- This psalm is related to the previous psalm, and was written after it because:

34.17.9.en: A - Both psalms speak of the angel of God and his work (Ps 34:7; 35:5-6). These two psalms are the only ones among the psalms that speak of the angel of God.

34.17.10.en: B - The previous psalm speaks of the afflictions of the righteous (ch. 34:19), and in this psalm he explains them in detail.

34.17.11.en: 4- Every section of this psalm ends with hope, so it is an encouraging psalm in the face of the enemies' cruelty.

34.17.12.en: 5- This psalm is an encouragement and support for the children of God in their afflictions; it is fitting for a person to repeat it when he meets an affliction.

34.17.13.en: 6- In this psalm David asks the just God to defend him, but at the same time he bears no hatred toward his enemies.

34.17.14.en: 7- This psalm is one of the Messianic psalms that speak of the sufferings that Christ met.

34.17.15.en: 8- Perhaps David, in the spirit of prophecy, felt what Jeremiah would suffer because of his enemies, and expressed that in this psalm (Jer 18:20, 22; 23:12).

34.17.16.en: 9- This psalm is not found in the Agpeya.
